```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
devtools::load_all(".")
chanwe_load_fonts()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 320)

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(42)

mt <- tibble::as_tibble(mtcars, rownames = "model") |>
  mutate(
    cyl = factor(cyl),
    gear = factor(gear),
    am = factor(am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual")),
    hp_band = cut(hp, breaks = c(-Inf, 110, 180, Inf), labels = c("Low", "Mid", "High"))
  )

econ <- economics |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2000-01-01")) |>
  mutate(unemp_pct = unemploy / pop * 100)

deltas <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("Revenue", "Gross margin", "EBITDA", "Opex", "Net income", "Churn"),
  actual = c(1240.5, 682.1, 310.2, -420.3, 185.7, 42.0),
  qoq = c(12.4, 4.2, -3.1, -1.9, 5.8, -0.8),
  yoy = c(28.1, 9.6, 11.2, 6.3, -2.4, -4.1)
)
```

# The Color System

Every color in `chanwer` is a named token. `chanwe_palette()` returns the
full inventory (130+ tokens in 21 groups); `chanwe_palette("<group>")`
returns one group; `chanwe_preview_palette("<group>")` draws its swatch
grid.

```r
chanwe_palette("chart")    # categorical 8, CVD-validated order
chanwe_palette("signed")   # canonical positive / negative / neutral
chanwe_palette("p15_teal") # one of eleven 5-shade brand family ramps
chanwe_palette("semantic") # roles: primary, success, danger, positive, ...
```

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="note" eyebrow="BRAND ROLES" title="The manual assigns each family a job"}
Coral is the house lead, blue is structural, green is positive, vermillion
is alert, ink is the neutral anchor. The scales below are built on those
roles — positive/negative is never an arbitrary red/green pair.
:::

## The categorical eight

Fixed slot order — coral, blue, teal, green, violet, magenta, mustard,
ink — validated for color-vision-deficiency separation (worst adjacent
pair ΔE 17.5 under protan/deutan simulation). Mustard and ink sit last
deliberately: charts with up to six series never reach them.

```{r}
#| label: preview-chart
#| fig-height: 3.4
chanwe_preview_palette("chart")
```

## The signed trio

Hue-true darkenings of the brand's positive (green), alert (vermillion),
and neutral (ink) families — stepped until each passes WCAG 4.5:1
small-text contrast on all five brand surfaces. The raw ramp poles do
not: bright green `#1EB508` tops out at 2.7:1.

```{r}
#| label: preview-signed
#| fig-height: 2.4
chanwe_preview_palette("signed")
```

## Family ramps

Eleven 5-shade brand families (`p15_*`), plus the main-brand 10-step
ramps (`mb_*`) and the legacy `p13_*` scales. Two examples:

```{r}
#| label: preview-teal
#| fig-height: 2.4
chanwe_preview_palette("p15_teal")
```

```{r}
#| label: preview-mb
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 3.4
chanwe_preview_palette("mb_orange")
```

# Categorical Scales

`scale_color_chanwe_d()` / `scale_fill_chanwe_d()` assign the chart
palette in slot order, recycling past eight.

```r
scale_color_chanwe_d()   # default: the categorical eight
```

```{r}
#| label: cat-scatter
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = hp_band)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_chanwe_d() +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Fuel economy by weight", eyebrow = "CATEGORICAL - 3 SERIES"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Scatter charts stay at three series or fewer"),
    x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "MPG", color = "HP band",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="warning" eyebrow="SERIES CAP" title="Scatter, bubble, and maps: three series maximum"}
In those forms any two marks can sit side by side, so the palette must
pass the stricter all-pairs check — the first three slots do. Fold extra
series into "Other" or facet. Bars, lines, and stacks may use up to six.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cat-bars
#| fig-height: 4.2
mpg_class <- ggplot2::mpg |>
  count(class) |>
  mutate(class = reorder(class, n))
ggplot(mpg_class, aes(n, class, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  scale_fill_chanwe_d() +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Vehicles by class", eyebrow = "CATEGORICAL - BARS"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Adjacent bars: up to six series before mustard and ink appear"),
    x = "Vehicles", y = NULL,
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::mpg")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

## Ordinal series take a one-hue ramp

When category order carries meaning (S/M/L, funnel stages, bands), use a
ramp group so the reader sees the order in the color.

```r
scale_fill_chanwe_d(palette = "p15_blue", reverse = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: ordinal
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(hp_band, fill = hp_band)) +
  geom_bar(width = 0.55) +
  scale_fill_chanwe_d(palette = "p15_blue", reverse = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Fleet by horsepower band", eyebrow = "ORDINAL - ONE HUE"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Low to High reads light to dark in a single family"),
    x = NULL, y = "Vehicles",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

# Sequential Scales

`scale_color_chanwe_c()` / `scale_fill_chanwe_c()` encode magnitude with
one-hue, light-to-dark brand gradients. Named ramps: `orange` (default),
`coral`, `blue`, `teal`, `green`, `vermillion`, `magenta`, `violet`,
`mustard`, `ink`. Green and vermillion end in the signed poles so the
dark end stays readable; yellow and cyan are deliberately not offered —
their whole family is too light to encode magnitude on brand surfaces.

```r
scale_color_chanwe_c(palette = "teal")
scale_fill_chanwe_c(palette = "green")   # dark pole = signed positive
```

```{r}
#| label: seq-teal
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = disp)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  scale_color_chanwe_c(palette = "teal") +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Displacement gradient", eyebrow = "SEQUENTIAL - TEAL"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("One hue, light to dark, magnitude only"),
    x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "MPG", color = "Disp.",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

```{r}
#| label: seq-orange
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(econ, aes(date, unemp_pct, color = psavert)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_chanwe_c() +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Unemployment, colored by savings rate", eyebrow = "SEQUENTIAL - ORANGE (DEFAULT)"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("The default gradient anchors on the report primary"),
    x = NULL, y = "Unemployment (%)", color = "Savings %",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::economics")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

# The Diverging Scale

`scale_color_chanwe_div()` / `scale_fill_chanwe_div()` encode polarity:
vermillion (negative) through a neutral gray midpoint to green
(positive), with the signed tokens at the poles. Give the scale
symmetric limits so zero lands exactly on the neutral midpoint.

```r
m <- max(abs(x))
scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-m, m))
```

```{r}
#| label: div-heat
#| fig-height: 3.6
heat <- expand.grid(week = 1:12, region = c("North", "Center", "West", "South"))
heat$delta <- round(rnorm(nrow(heat), 0, 2) + rep(c(1.4, 0.3, -0.6, -1.5), each = 12), 1)
m <- max(abs(heat$delta))
ggplot(heat, aes(week, region, fill = delta)) +
  geom_tile(color = "#F7F7F7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-m, m)) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Weekly delta vs plan", eyebrow = "DIVERGING - HEATMAP"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Symmetric limits pin zero to the neutral midpoint"),
    x = "Week", y = NULL, fill = "Δ pp",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: simulated")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

```{r}
#| label: div-bars
#| fig-height: 4.2
mk <- ggplot2::mpg |>
  group_by(manufacturer) |>
  summarise(hwy = mean(hwy), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(delta = hwy - mean(hwy), manufacturer = reorder(manufacturer, delta))
md <- max(abs(mk$delta))
ggplot(mk, aes(delta, manufacturer, fill = delta)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-md, md)) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Highway MPG vs fleet average", eyebrow = "DIVERGING - BARS"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Above average in green, below in vermillion"),
    x = "Δ MPG", y = NULL,
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::mpg")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

## KPI scoreboard

`chanwe_kpi()` wrapped in `chanwe_subtitle()` inserts the scoreboard
between subtitle and chart; the ▲/▼ arrows wear the signed tokens.

```r
chanwe_subtitle("Reservas internacionales brutas",
  kpi = chanwe_kpi(num = "45,91", label = "USD MM", period = "05·MAY·2026",
                   mtc1_num = "0,19%", mtc1_label = "WoW", mtc1_direction = "+", ...))
```

```{r}
#| label: kpi-plot
#| fig-height: 4.4
ggplot(econ, aes(date, unemp_pct)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = chanwe_palette("chart")[["chart-blue"]]) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Unemployment rate", eyebrow = "SIGNED - KPI SCOREBOARD"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
      "Share of population, monthly",
      kpi = chanwe_kpi(
        num = "3,9", label = "PCT", period = "APR·2015",
        mtc1_num = "0,1pp", mtc1_label = "MoM", mtc1_direction = "-",
        mtc2_num = "0,4pp", mtc2_label = "QoQ", mtc2_direction = "-",
        mtc3_num = "1,1pp", mtc3_label = "YoY", mtc3_direction = "+"
      )
    ),
    x = NULL, y = "%",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::economics")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

## Signed deltas in tables

`chanwe_col_signed()` is a ready-made `col_colors` function. Color
functions receive the column's *raw* values (before `fmt`), so sign
logic works even when the column renders as text.

```r
chanwe_kbl(df,
  fmt        = list(qoq = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)),
  col_colors = list(qoq = chanwe_col_signed()))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-signed
chanwe_kbl(
  deltas,
  title = "Quarterly performance",
  subtitle = "Signed deltas via chanwe_col_signed() - raw values drive the color while fmt renders the text",
  eyebrow = "SIGNED - TABLES",
  caption = "Source: finance close, Q1 - simulated",
  col_labels = c(metric = "Metric", actual = "USD K", qoq = "QoQ", yoy = "YoY"),
  stub = "metric",
  fmt = list(
    actual = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
    qoq = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x),
    yoy = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)
  ),
  col_colors = list(
    qoq = chanwe_col_signed(),
    yoy = chanwe_col_signed()
  )
)
```

# Theme Variants

`theme_chanwe()` exposes five named surfaces (plus `"transparent"` and
raw hex); grid colors adapt per surface.

```r
theme_chanwe()                        # "metallic" #F7F7F7 (default)
theme_chanwe(bg_color = "beige")      # #F5F1EB
theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white")      # #FFFFFF
theme_chanwe(bg_color = "gray")       # #EDF0F1
theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white-ivory")# #FAF9F7
```

```{r}
#| label: bg-beige
#| fig-height: 3.6
p_bg <- ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = cyl)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_color_chanwe_d() +
  labs(x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = "Cyl",
       caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars"))
p_bg +
  labs(title = chanwe_title("Beige surface", eyebrow = "THEME - BG"),
       subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('theme_chanwe(bg_color = "beige")')) +
  theme_chanwe(bg_color = "beige")
```

```{r}
#| label: bg-white
#| fig-height: 3.6
p_bg +
  labs(title = chanwe_title("Paper white surface", eyebrow = "THEME - BG"),
       subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white")')) +
  theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white")
```

```{r}
#| label: bg-gray
#| fig-height: 3.6
p_bg +
  labs(title = chanwe_title("Gray surface", eyebrow = "THEME - BG"),
       subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('theme_chanwe(bg_color = "gray")')) +
  theme_chanwe(bg_color = "gray")
```

## Header spacing and rules

```{r}
#| label: no-subtitle
#| fig-height: 3.4
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, color = chanwe_palette("chart")[["chart-coral"]]) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("No subtitle mode", eyebrow = "THEME - HAS_SUBTITLE = FALSE"),
    x = "Weight", y = "MPG",
    caption = chanwe_caption("The title grob draws its own separator line")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(has_subtitle = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: no-headerline
#| fig-height: 3.4
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, color = chanwe_palette("chart")[["chart-blue"]]) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Minimal header", eyebrow = "THEME - HEADER_LINE = FALSE"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("No separator rule - for embedded layouts"),
    x = "Weight", y = "MPG",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(header_line = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: borders
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, color = chanwe_palette("chart")[["chart-teal"]]) +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Framed plot", eyebrow = "THEME - PLOT_BORDERS"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('plot_borders = "top_bottom" adds thin ink frame lines'),
    x = "Weight", y = "MPG",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe(plot_borders = "top_bottom")
```

## Subtitle with a note line

```{r}
#| label: subtitle-note
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = am)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_color_chanwe_d() +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Transmission comparison", eyebrow = "HEADER - NOTE LINE"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
      "Linear fit per transmission type",
      note = "Excludes exotics; n = 32; OLS with no interaction terms"
    ),
    x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = NULL,
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

## Faceting

```{r}
#| label: facets
#| fig-height: 4.6
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = cyl)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.0) +
  facet_wrap(~am) +
  scale_color_chanwe_d() +
  labs(
    title = chanwe_title("Faceted by transmission", eyebrow = "THEME - FACETS"),
    subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Strip labels in JetBrains Mono Thin"),
    x = "Weight", y = "MPG", color = "Cyl",
    caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
  ) +
  theme_chanwe()
```

# Typst Tables

`chanwe_kbl()` generates native Typst — no HTML-to-PDF translation
losses. Both densities, every background, per-column formatting and
coloring, stubs, totals, highlights, and vertical rules.

## Densities

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spacious
cyl_summary <- mt |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarise(avg_mpg = mean(mpg), avg_hp = mean(hp), avg_wt = mean(wt), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

chanwe_kbl(
  cyl_summary,
  title = "Fleet summary by cylinder count",
  subtitle = "Spacious density - the presentation default",
  eyebrow = "TABLES - SPACIOUS",
  caption = "Source: mtcars",
  col_labels = c(cyl = "Cylinders", avg_mpg = "Avg MPG", avg_hp = "Avg HP", avg_wt = "Avg weight", n = "Vehicles"),
  fmt = list(
    avg_mpg = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x),
    avg_hp = function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x),
    avg_wt = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
  ),
  density = "spacious"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compact
chanwe_kbl(
  head(mt |> select(model, mpg, cyl, hp, wt, am), 8),
  title = "Vehicle detail",
  subtitle = "Compact density for dense reporting tables",
  eyebrow = "TABLES - COMPACT",
  caption = "Source: mtcars",
  col_labels = c(model = "Model", mpg = "MPG", cyl = "Cyl", hp = "HP", wt = "Weight", am = "Transmission"),
  stub = "model",
  density = "compact",
  bg = "beige"
)
```

## Totals, highlights, and rules

```{r}
#| label: tbl-totals
region_rev <- tibble::tibble(
  region = c("North", "Center", "West", "South", "Total"),
  q1 = c(412.1, 388.4, 251.9, 188.1, 1240.5),
  q2 = c(438.0, 371.2, 266.3, 201.5, 1277.0),
  delta = c(6.3, -4.4, 5.7, 7.1, 2.9)
)

chanwe_kbl(
  region_rev,
  title = "Revenue by region",
  subtitle = "Total row via n_total; QoQ column highlighted and signed; vline separates quarters from the delta",
  eyebrow = "TABLES - TOTALS + HIGHLIGHT",
  caption = "Source: finance close - simulated",
  col_labels = c(region = "Region", q1 = "Q1 USD K", q2 = "Q2 USD K", delta = "QoQ %"),
  stub = "region",
  fmt = list(
    q1 = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
    q2 = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
    delta = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)
  ),
  col_colors = list(delta = chanwe_col_signed()),
  n_total = 1,
  highlight_cols = 4,
  vlines = 3,
  bg = "white-ivory"
)
```

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="success" eyebrow="ONE SYSTEM" title="The same tokens, everywhere"}
The QoQ column above, the KPI arrows in section 5, and the diverging
heatmap poles in section 4 are the exact same three hexes —
`chanwe_palette("signed")`. Change them once, and every chart, table,
and report follows.
:::
